candidates.title: Port of Hueneme advances container export plans amid auto cargo decline
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Hueneme is developing a new container export initiative targeting agricultural shipments from California to Asian markets, as the port seeks to diversify cargo activity following a decline in automobile volumes. The initiative was outlined during the port’s 2026 State of the Port presentation, held in late October and detailed in an announcement issued on 2 November. According to the port, automobile volumes fell by 13% during the latest fiscal year, with tariffs contributing to the decline. However, higher high-and-heavy cargo volumes and a slight increase in container imports helped support its overall financial performance. The proposed export initiative aims to use available container capacity to transport agricultural products from Ventura County to Asian markets. The port has not disclosed a launch date, expected shipment volumes or specific shipping partners. candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic increased 7.8% in the week ended Oct. 24 compared with the same week in 2025, as growth in intermodal shipments outpaced gains in carloads, Association of American Railroads data shows. Weekly intermodal volume, which includes containers and trailers, rose 11.3%, while carload traffic increased 3.6%. Both measures grew faster than their respective year-to-date rates. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded year-over-year increases. Petroleum and petroleum products led percentage growth, rising 15.4%, followed by motor vehicles and parts at 15.3%. Forest products increased 11.7%, and metallic ores and metals gained 11.6%. Farm products excluding grain, and food fell 3.7%, while grain posted a rare decline at 1.4%. For the first 42 weeks of 2026, combined U.S. rail traffic increased 3.8% from the same period in 2025. Carloads rose 2.7%, while intermodal traffic was better by 4.7%.
